title: NAFv4.1 · UAF-based structural application profile
description: All 47 NAFv4.1 (2026.03) viewpoint IDs with executable structural checks, inherited UAF 1.0 types and explicit application adapters. Use @help viewpoints naf41-uaf ID and @help connections naf41-uaf TYPE.
sources: ReferenceDocs/nafv4/NAFv4-ADMBw-MDG-2026.05.xml — supporting comparison only; its declared foundation is NAF 4.0
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
No certification or complete NAF/UAF conformance is claimed. All 47 IDs are covered structurally, not all normative semantics.
The inherited UAF coverage report still applies, including deferred native constraints. Application adapters are identified in type help.
Only included view elements/links count toward viewpoint connection rules. Typed references resolve in the model; designated structural references must also be visible.
NAF methodology, stakeholder approval, full state/sequence execution semantics and qualitative completeness require human review. See profiles/naf41/COVERAGE.md.

Service.description: NAF S1 vocabulary resolved to UAF 1.0 ServiceSpecification in this application profile. ActualService remains distinct.
limitations: UAF 1.2 renamed ServiceSpecification to Service alongside other service metamodel changes. This alias retains UAF 1.0 semantics; it does not claim cross-version equivalence.

Node.description: NAF S2/L1/L4 Node vocabulary for the existing logical-node application type. Its UAF projection is OperationalArchitecture through LogicalNode.
limitations: Explicit arch.js application mapping. This is not a native UAF or ADMBw stereotype named Node, nor an assertion that every OperationalArchitecture must be called Node.

Role.description: NAF L4 vocabulary for a role held by a logical Node. The application profile resolves Role to the UAF 1.0 OperationalRole type.
limitations: HoldsRole and PerformsOperationalActivity express the explicit links in the NAF example. Native UAF role ownership and action-level execution semantics are outside this projection.

PhysicalActiveResource.description: Abstract NAF physical active resource category mapped to UAF ResourcePerformer. Use a concrete subtype such as System for the S2 air traffic control system. Set stereotype "Physical Active Resource" to reproduce the caption in the example.
limitations: The application alias covers the full ResourcePerformer hierarchy. Models instantiating the former concrete adapter can pin naf41-uaf@4.1.0-arch.33.

ServiceOperation.description: NAF S3 operation vocabulary resolved to UAF 1.0 ServiceMethod, which extends UML Operation. This alias retains the native runtime rules and written source name.
limitations: Application vocabulary mapping, not a claim that all native UML operation-owner, method and ownedParameter constraints are implemented.

ResourceFunction.description: NAF Resource Function vocabulary resolved to UAF 1.0 Function. The written name is preserved in the model and diagram.

PostType.description: P2 vocabulary for a type of post. The native UAF Post supplies the resource semantics.

ArchitectureDescription.description: NAF Architecture Description vocabulary from the A1 cut-out and example, resolved to UAF 1.0 ArchitecturalDescription in this application profile.

C2.title: Enterprise Vision
C2.description: Vision, goals, enterprise phases and capabilities linked to them.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
EnterprisePhase is the required planning-phase representation in this mapping; ActualEnterprisePhase can additionally record actual states.

The C2 cut-out permits desires from an enterprise phase to a capability, vision or goal. Every planning phase requires at least one of these links; a direct DesiresCapability is not mandatory when DesiresVision/DesiresGoal is present.

C7.title: Performance Criteria
C7.description: Capabilities characterized by assessment criteria evaluated by measures, with optional effectiveness criteria.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

EffectivenessCriterion and its subtypes are excluded from the per-assessment-criterion mandatory characterization/evaluation checks. Their links are optional, following p.98 and the Time to find example on p.99. Ordinary assessment criteria still require the complete capability-criterion-measure chain.

EvaluatesCriterion is directed from Measure to AssessmentCriterion, following the p.98 cut-out. The evaluates arrows on p.99 are drawn in the opposite direction; that illustration does not change endpoint compatibility.

Cr.title: Capability Roadmap
Cr.description: Increments deliver capabilities and may relate to planning phases with temporal grouping and trigger dependencies. Supports the p.103 presentation with implicit milestone properties.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

The p.103 example omits explicit milestone nodes because milestones are properties of an increment. Cr therefore does not require visible CapabilityMilestone nodes or incoming DefinesIncrement at every increment. Explicit visible milestones still require a DefinesIncrement link; the optional milestones reference attribute may point to model elements outside the view. Implicit milestone completeness is not checked.

AggregatesEnterprisePhase and TriggersEnterprisePhase are authored binary application adapters, directed whole-to-part and triggering-to-following phase. Each type is acyclic and disallows self-links as an application rule. No single-parent ownership, UML TemporalPart/slot semantics, execution, guards or date ordering between phases is inferred.

CapabilityIncrement is a distinct UAFElement adapter, not an ActualEnterprisePhase/Achiever/ActualState. Earlier implicit compatibility with AchievedEffect and ActualEnterprisePhase relationships no longer applies. Optional startDate/endDate retain ISO date-time validation and ordering.
Connected views reproduce the explanatory p.103 structure. A time-based Gantt representation needs actual schedule dates; the sample does not invent them.
representations: NAF formats: Gantt-style chart
arch.js: timeline, connected for the example structure
Plot ranges and milestones with explicit dates.

S1.title: Service Taxonomy
S1.description: Service specialization taxonomy. Service is a vocabulary alias of UAF 1.0 ServiceSpecification in this application profile; policies and nested groups are optional context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Service aliases ServiceSpecification in both directions, preserving written labels and inherited service rules. This is not an implementation of the UAF 1.2 service metamodel. ServiceGeneralization points from the specialized service to its general service. Multiple inheritance is permitted by the profile; a whole-view tree still requires one hierarchy parent per node.

SatisfiesServicePolicy points from service to policy, following pp.104–105. ServicePolicySatisfiedBy is the retained inverse application link, not a direction change to existing models. Native ServicePolicy still requires its ruleKind attribute; the p.105 drawing does not specify that value.

GroupsService connects a ServiceGroup to a member service; AggregatesServiceGroup connects a group to a member group. The latter disallows self-links/cycles as an application rule, without imposing single-parent ownership or strong composition.
Use a Connected view with a ServiceGeneralization-only tree group when policy/group context is present. A whole-view tree may filter to ServiceGeneralization, omitting non-hierarchy edges.
representations: NAF formats: Tables, hierarchy and class diagrams
arch.js: table, tree, class

S2.title: Service Structure
S2.description: Service aggregation, composition and dependencies; optional interfaces, functions, logical nodes and physical realizations.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Node is an alias of the application LogicalNode, a subtype of OperationalArchitecture. This models the logical grouping/architecture meaning of a NAF Node, not a physical System, runtime instance or drawing template.

The pp.107–108 directions are node to service (ConsumesService), function to service (EnablesService), and physical active resource to service (RealizesService). Native Consumes, IsCapableToPerform and Implements are unchanged; they are not interchangeable aliases of these adapters.

ServiceAggregation projects whole service to member service (aggregates in the source), with a solid directed link and no exclusive ownership. ServiceComposition remains a separate relationship with composition notation. Both reject cycles/self-links; full UML ownership/lifecycle semantics are not implemented. ServiceDependency remains dependent service to required service.

Per-service structural checks count ServiceAggregation/ServiceComposition/ServiceDependency, not optional node/function/resource traces. Optional provider and consumer roles may provide or consume the same service and rely on a logical Node. The Node can independently deliver or consume a service.
representations: NAF formats: Tables, matrices, dependency graphs and diagrams
arch.js: table, matrix, connected

S3.title: Service Interfaces
S3.description: Services specify interfaces and optional operations with shared conceptual parameters and optional physical data-product traces.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

ServiceOperation is an application-profile vocabulary alias of UAF ServiceMethod (a UML Operation stereotype). DataProductType is a separate DataElement/PhysicalPassiveResource specialization. Native UAF and ADMBw definitions are unchanged.

HasServiceOperationParameter runs from operation to parameter; InvolvesPhysicalResource runs from parameter to a physical passive resource/data product. The p.110 Geographic Location parameter is shared by two operations. These are conceptual associations, not exclusive UML Parameter ownership.

Legacy owner/resource references remain valid. Owners must be visible; resource traces may be omitted in S3. An owner reference can satisfy the required operation association instead of a has link; identical link/reference evidence is counted once. S3 does not require a resource for every parameter, matching the Resource parameter in p.110.

An optional DataModel trace uses SpecifiesData from model to DataElement/DataProductType. A parameter does not link directly to a DataModel. Full UML operation signatures, parameter ordering/directions and consistency between simultaneous link/reference declarations require review.
representations: NAF formats: Tables and diagrams
arch.js: table, connected, class

S4.title: Service Functions
S4.description: Functions enabling services, recursive function aggregation, provider/consumer roles and operational activity context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Each selected function must enable a selected service directly or through selected aggregating ancestors. Legacy service-to-function IsCapableToPerform remains accepted. This is contextual coverage, not inheritance of behavior or implicit model edges.

Provider and consumer are explicit contextual application roles, with optional represents references. Cut-out links are directed structural projections; no execution, notification delivery, exclusive ownership or full UML activity decomposition is asserted.
representations: NAF formats: Tables and diagrams
arch.js: table, connected, tree

S5.title: Service States
S5.description: States, objectified or compact transitions, events, functions, modes and state groupings.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

The transition node and edge share a type name in separate namespaces. Bind the object node via the edge transition attribute; is equal to is the graphical reference connector, not a separate edge with an edge ID as endpoint. Each selected transition object binds exactly one selected state edge.

Legacy owner/function/event references remain accepted. State/mode ownership is checked in S5 through an explicit link or selected reference; duplicate contradictory ownership is rejected. Cross-state same-service consistency, conflicting event representations, guards, reachability, execution and omitted model elements require review.
representations: NAF formats: Diagrams and state diagrams
arch.js: connected, state

S6.title: Service Sequence
S6.description: Ordered compact or objectified interactions between lifelines, with optional service/function/interface/operation/event context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Interaction objects bind exactly one selected lifeline message; message endpoints belong to the edge. Lifelines represent services and are not objectified interactions. Compact event/operation/represents references remain supported; explicit context links are optional.

Sequence views support object cards and is equal to attachments. showContext true draws other selected cards and relationships in a context area. orderAttribute order sorts and checks unique positive message positions; otherwise declaration order or an explicit messages list determines display order. No execution, temporal constraints, UML fragments or event/operation-reference consistency is asserted.
representations: NAF formats: Sequence diagrams
arch.js: sequence, connected for the example structure

S7.title: Service Interface Parameters
S7.description: Operation/function parameters reference their owner and passive resource.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Use ServiceOperationParameter or ServiceFunctionParameter: the unqualified UAF ServiceParameter lacks the required owner/payload projection. Both parameter kinds may use explicit has/involves links or owner/resource references. S7 requires owner association and visibility of known resource mappings; missing model mappings are non-blocking review notices; function parameters involve logical OperationalExchangeItems, while operation parameters involve physical resources. Legacy physical function-parameter references remain accepted. S3 makes the operation resource trace optional.
representations: NAF formats: Tables and diagrams
arch.js: table, connected, class

L1.title: Logical Taxonomy
L1.description: Logical nodes organize relevant active resources, behavior and optional passive resources, following the pp.126–127 taxonomy.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
LogicalActor and LogicalEquipment are distinct concrete application subtypes of OperationalPerformer, not aliases or native UAF 1.0 stereotypes.

Grouping and specialization nodes do not each require a direct performer or activity. The p.127 example contains no activity; single-node taxonomies are accepted. Which resources/behavior are relevant and whether all relevant elements are present require review.

Selected active resources require node grouping directly or through selected OperationalGeneralization ancestors. Selected behavior can inherit grouping via LogicalBehaviorGeneralization. Selected passive resources require an incoming GroupsLogicalResource from a node. Capability traces and passive resources are optional; existing UAF types remain supported.
representations: NAF formats: Connected shapes and tables
arch.js: tree, connected, table

L2.title: Logical Structure
L2.description: Logical nodes connected by compact or objectified Needlines, with optional conveyed resources.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Needline is both a node and relationship name in separate namespaces. Compact edges need no object card; the edge needline attribute binds the optional object and draws is equal to. An object can be omitted from a view without removing its Needline edge.

Each selected Needline object requires one selected bound edge or a complete legacy source/target pair with selected endpoints. Binding is unique across the model; simultaneous endpoint references must match the edge. Legacy references do not synthesize extra model edges or their visualization.

At least one Needline edge or complete legacy object is required; LogicalDependency alone is not a substitute. Conveyed resources and their ConveysLogicalResource links are optional presentation context, including when known mappings exist. Structural hierarchy uses GroupsLogicalResource. Payload completeness, transport details and full UML association-class semantics require review.
representations: NAF formats: Connected shapes, composite structure and rich pictures
arch.js: connected with packages, images and icons

L2-L3.title: Logical Concept
L2-L3.description: Informal high-level concept: no mandatory information-model content.

L3.title: Logical Interactions
L3.description: Logical interactions carry passive logical resources. Needlines and their logical nodes are optional context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

The p.131 cut-out permits optional Needline edges, their object cards, logical Node endpoints, and requested resources. Nodes shown for structure or needline context do not each require a LogicalInteraction.

Supply at least one selected payload via the conveyed attribute or a ConveysLogicalResource link from the bound interaction object. Needline resource context is optional. The needline reference points to the Needline object.

An interaction object can bind to its carrying edge and trace to a Needline or convey a logical resource. Compact edges can record selected payloads directly. The optional volume attribute can drive a weighted Sankey diagram.
representations: NAF formats: Tables, information-flow diagrams and Sankey diagrams
arch.js: table, connected, sankey
Sankey uses acyclic directed links and an optional numeric weight.

L4.title: Logical Activities
L4.description: Control flows, activity allocations and optional resource flows, events and traces.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Role is an application vocabulary alias of UAF 1.0 OperationalRole. HoldsRole represents its logical Node context when both appear in the view. Roles can be shown without their holding Nodes in an activity-focused view.
Each selected activity requires a visible incoming allocation from a Node, Role or legacy OperationalAgent. Native IsCapableToPerform remains available for OperationalAgent allocations.

OperationalFlow is optional and separate from the required control flow. Its optional object card binds to one selected edge via flow. Payload resources and conveys links may be omitted from the view. LogicalObjectFlow still uses a typed conveyed list.
representations: NAF formats: Hierarchies, activity, process and collaboration diagrams
arch.js: tree, activity with optional swimlanes, connected

L5.title: Logical States
L5.description: States of logical active resources, compact or objectified transitions, events, activities, functions, modes and state groups.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
Connected diagrams draw compact event triggers on state-to-state edges and attach objectified transitions through the transition reference. Event visibility is optional.
State-machine execution, cross-owner transitions, consistency between compact and objectified triggers, and guard completeness require review.
representations: NAF formats: Connected shapes and finite state/transition diagrams
arch.js: connected, state

L6.title: Logical Sequence
L6.description: Ordered interactions between lifelines representing logical active resources.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
Each selected lifeline represents exactly one selected logical active resource through an explicit relationship or a compact reference.
LogicalSequenceInteraction supports compact event and activity references. Bind a LogicalInteraction object to the message to show explicit event and behavior links.
Interaction fragments and concurrency require review. Use orderAttribute order to sort and validate message order in a sequence diagram.
representations: NAF formats: Sequence, event trace and timing diagrams
arch.js: sequence, connected
Relative sequence order is supported. Use a separate dated timeline for real timestamps.

L7.title: Information Model
L7.description: Information entities with optional model, product and typed attributes.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
InformationEntity specializes InformationElement. Both satisfy the entity requirement and can be specified by an InformationModel.
RepresentsInformationProduct follows the scope and cut-out on p.141. The reversed arrow in the p.142 example is treated as a likely editorial error.
An included attribute belongs to one visible entity. Attribute types can be omitted from the view. Compact owner and attributeType references remain valid.
representations: NAF formats: Entity–relationship and class diagrams
arch.js: class, connected
Draw typed associations and properties. Crow’s-foot multiplicity notation remains open.

L8.title: Logical Constraints
L8.description: Logical constraints and requirements apply to logical resources or behavior.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

A requirement can relate to a constraint as in the cut-out, or apply directly to a logical subject as in the p.144 example. The example omits explicit requirement-to-constraint links; sharing a subject does not establish such a link.
LogicalConstraint specializes OperationalConstraint. Its declared type implies ruleKind Constraint. The native OperationalConstraint retains its required ruleKind.
representations: NAF formats: Statements, business rules, matrices and parametric diagrams
arch.js: table for structured rules, matrix, connected
Human review is required for rule interpretation.

Lr.title: Logical Roadmap

The cut-out and example use LogicalReadinessFulfilsResource from readiness level to resource. Existing models can use the inverse FulfilsLogicalReadiness direction. Either link satisfies the readiness association.
DefinesLogicalEvolution and SchedulesLogical describe optional project context. The example on p.146 leaves dates open; LogicalMilestone requires an ISO date in this profile.

CapabilityGroupDependency.description: Dependent capability group to required capability group.

SupportsEnduringTask.description: Capability to the enduring task it supports.

GoalRelatesEnduringTask.description: Goal to a related enduring task.

DesiresVision.description: Enterprise phase to desired vision, as shown in the C2 cut-out and the p.91 example.

DesiresGoal.description: Enterprise phase to desired goal, as shown in the C2 cut-out.

CharacterizesCapability.description: Performance criterion to the capability characterized, following the C7 cut-out direction.

CharacterizesEffect.description: Effectiveness criterion to the effect assessed.

ConstrainsCapability.description: Planning constraint to the capability constrained.

OriginatesFromRationale.description: Constraint to its originating rationale, following the C8 cut-out. JustifiesStrategy remains the explicit inverse application relationship.

RelatesToEnterprisePhase.description: Capability increment to a related planning enterprise phase, following the Cr cut-out and p.103 example. Distinct from AchievedEffect, whose target must be an ActualState.

AggregatesEnterprisePhase.description: Whole planning phase to a temporal subphase, following aggregates on pp.102–103. Binary application projection of temporal membership, not an imported UAF TemporalPart property or UML composition.

TriggersEnterprisePhase.description: Triggering planning phase to a following phase, following triggers on pp.102–103. A directed planning dependency, not an executable state transition or a calculated date constraint.

DefinesCapabilityEvolution.description: Capability project to the capability whose evolution it defines.

ConfigurationRealizesCapability.description: Capability configuration to the capability it realizes.

ServiceAggregation.description: Whole service to a member service, following aggregates in the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. A separate directed grouping relation, not an alias of ServiceComposition and not exclusive composition ownership.
limitations: Binary application projection rendered as a solid directed link. Self-links/cycles are disallowed; multiple aggregating services may reference the same member. Full UML shared-aggregation, ownership and lifecycle semantics are not implemented.

ServiceDependency.description: Dependent service to required service. Restricted service-to-service subset of the ADMBw relationship.

ConsumesService.description: Logical node or explicit S4 consumer role to the service it consumes. Native UAF Consumes remains OperationalActivity to ServiceSpecification.

EnablesService.description: Service function to the service it enables, following the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. The native IsCapableToPerform relation remains service to function.

RealizesService.description: Physical active resource to the service it realizes, following the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. Native Implements retains its UAF endpoint pairs.

ServiceFunctionAggregation.description: Whole function to constituent function. Shared membership is permitted; not UML exclusive ownership or executable activity decomposition.

ProvidesService.description: Provider role to the service it provides.

DeliversService.description: Logical Node to the service it delivers.

ServiceRoleReliesOnNode.description: Explicit provider or consumer role to the logical Node it relies on.

NotifiesServiceProvider.description: Service function to the provider role it notifies.

AccessesServiceFunction.description: Consumer role to the function it accesses.

SupportsServiceFunction.description: Operational activity to the function it supports. Distinct from the inverse enables projection.

EnablesOperationalActivity.description: Service function or physical active resource to the operational activity it enables.

PerformsOperationalActivity.description: Service provider, service consumer, logical Node or Role to the operational activity it performs. Native IsCapableToPerform retains its existing endpoint rules.

AggregatesServiceGroup.description: Whole service group to a member group, following the recursive grouping in the S1 cut-out. Acyclic binary membership projection, not strong UML composition.

HasServiceOperationParameter.description: Service operation to its conceptual parameter, following has on pp.109–110. The same parameter may be associated with multiple operations; this is not UML exclusive ownership.

HasServiceFunctionParameter.description: Service function to its conceptual parameter, following the has association on pp.119–120.

InvolvesLogicalResource.description: Service function parameter to a logical passive resource, including InformationProduct or InformationElement, following pp.119–120. Uses the native UAF OperationalExchangeItem category; physical data products are not valid targets.

InvolvesPhysicalResource.description: Service operation parameter to the physical passive resource or data product it involves, following pp.109–110. Data Model trace is indirect through that resource; DataModel is not a valid direct target.

ServicePolicySatisfiedBy.description: Policy to a service satisfying it. Retained inverse application relationship; use SatisfiesServicePolicy for the service-to-policy direction shown on pp.104–105.

SatisfiesServicePolicy.description: Service to the policy it satisfies, following the S1 cut-out and p.105 example. ServicePolicySatisfiedBy remains the explicit inverse application relationship.

ServiceStateTransition.description: Source state to target state. An optional transition reference binds its objectified form; an optional event retains the legacy compact representation.

HasServiceState.description: Service to one of its states.

TriggersServiceStateTransition.description: Service event to the objectified transition it triggers.

StateEnablesServiceFunction.description: Service state to a function it enables.

HasServiceMode.description: Service function to one of its modes.

GroupsServiceState.description: State group to a member state.

AggregatesServiceStateGroup.description: State group to a nested state group. Shared grouping, not exclusive UML ownership.

ServiceInteraction.description: Ordered message between service lifelines; interaction binds the optional objectified form. Compact event/operation references remain valid.

RepresentsService.description: Lifeline to the service whose timeline it represents.

TriggersServiceInteraction.description: Event to the objectified interaction it triggers.

InteractionRelatesOperation.description: Objectified interaction to a related service operation.

DefinesServiceEvolution.description: Service project to the service whose evolution it defines.

GroupsLogicalResource.description: Logical node to the resources/behavior it groups.

NeedsCapability.description: Logical Node to a capability it needs. Exhibits retains its separate capability-support mapping.

LogicalBehaviorGeneralization.description: A specialized logical behavior to a more general behavior of the same kind.

Needline.description: Need for key or aggregated exchanges between logical nodes. An optional needline reference binds the objectified form. L2 shows the logical structure; L3 can show the same Needline as context.

ConveysLogicalResource.description: Objectified needline, operational flow or logical interaction to its logical payload.

RealizesNeedline.description: Objectified logical interaction to the needline it realizes.

LogicalDependency.description: Logical structural dependency. A Needline is modeled separately.

LogicalInteraction.description: Logical interaction with a typed payload. The optional interaction binds its object representation. The default connected presentation uses reference cards attached to the flow, following the example on page 132 with the original arch.js templates and colors.

HoldsRole.description: Logical Node to a Role held in its context.

LogicalControlFlow.description: Control flow between operational activity definitions, as shown in L4. The NAF profile also accepts OperationalControlFlow for these endpoints.

LogicalObjectFlow.description: Flow of logical passive resources between activity definitions.

OperationalFlow.description: Flow between operational activity definitions. The optional flow reference binds the objectified form for a captioned is equal to connector.

OperationalActivityAggregation.description: Whole operational activity to a constituent activity.

ActsUponLogicalResource.description: Operational activity to a logical passive resource it acts upon.

TriggersOperationalActivity.description: Logical event to the operational activity it triggers.

TriggersLogicalEvent.description: Operational activity to the logical event it triggers.

RelatesServiceToOperationalActivity.description: Service to a related operational activity, following the L4 cut-out direction.

LogicalStateTransition.description: Source state to target state. Use event for a compact trigger and transition to bind the objectified form.

HasLogicalState.description: Logical active resource, including a Node or LogicalActor, to one of its states.

TriggersLogicalTransition.description: Logical event to the objectified transition it triggers.

StateEnablesOperationalActivity.description: Logical state to an operational activity it enables.

StateEnablesLogicalFunction.description: Logical state to a logical function it enables.

HasLogicalMode.description: Operational activity or logical function to one of its modes.

GroupsLogicalState.description: Logical state group to a member state.

AggregatesLogicalStateGroup.description: Logical state group to a nested group.

RepresentsLogicalResource.description: Lifeline to the logical active resource whose timeline it represents, following the L6 cut-out and example.

TriggersLogicalInteraction.description: A logical event triggers an objectified interaction.

LogicalInteractionRelatesBehavior.description: Objectified interaction to its logical function or operational activity.

SpecifiesInformation.description: Information model to an information entity or legacy InformationElement.

RepresentsInformationProduct.description: Information model to represented product, following the L7 scope and cut-out.

AggregatesInformationAttribute.description: Information entity to one of its attributes, following the L7 cut-out.

HasInformationAttributeType.description: Information attribute to its type, following the L7 cut-out.

ConstrainsLogical.description: Logical constraint or requirement to the logical resource or behavior it applies to.

TracesStrategicConstraint.description: Logical constraint to strategic constraint traced.

OriginatesFromLogicalRationale.description: Logical constraint to its originating rationale, following the L8 cut-out.

OriginatesFromStrategicConstraint.description: Logical rationale to the strategic constraint it originates from, following the L8 cut-out.

LogicalReadinessFulfilsResource.description: Readiness level to the logical active resource it fulfils, as drawn in the Lr cut-out and example.

FulfilsLogicalReadiness.description: Legacy inverse direction from the logical active resource to its readiness level. For the NAF arrow direction use LogicalReadinessFulfilsResource.

TracesCapabilityIncrement.description: Logical readiness to capability increment traced.

DefinesLogicalEvolution.description: Logical project to the logical active resource whose evolution it defines.

GroupsPhysicalResource.description: Capability configuration to member active/passive resource.

PhysicalDependency.description: Physical active resource to required active/passive resource.

ResourceAggregation.description: Whole physical active resource to an aggregated active resource.

ResourceFunctionAggregation.description: Whole resource function to a constituent resource function.

UsesResourceFunction.description: A physical active resource uses a resource function. The performs allocation is modeled with IsCapableToPerform.

RealizesLogicalFunction.description: Resource function to the logical function it realizes. Use UAF Implements for traces to a service function or operational activity.

InteractionConformsTo.description: Interaction to governing standard/protocol. Protocol is a UAF Standard subtype.

ResourceImplementsProtocol.description: Resource to implemented protocol; direct projection, not ADMBw ProtocolImplementation reification.

FunctionalFlow.description: Control flow between function definitions (not action-level FunctionControlFlow).

ResourceInteraction.description: Interaction between physical active resources. Bind its optional object card through interaction.

PassiveResourceAggregation.description: Whole physical passive resource to its part.

RealizesLogicalInteraction.description: Objectified physical interaction to its logical trace.

RealizesLogicalResource.description: Physical passive resource to the logical passive resource it realizes.

ConveysPhysicalResource.description: An objectified physical interaction or flow to its conveyed resource.

ResourceFlow.description: Passive-resource flow between function definitions. A payload or bound flow object may be supplied.

ResourceStateTransition.description: Source state to target state. Optionally bind a transition object or record a triggering event.

HasResourceState.description: Physical active resource to a state it can occupy.

HasResourceMode.description: Resource function to one of its modes.

GroupsResourceState.description: Resource state group to a member state or group.

StateEnablesResourceFunction.description: A resource state enables a resource function.

ResourceStateRelatesLogicalState.description: Resource state to a related logical state.

TriggersResourceTransition.description: Resource event to the objectified transition it triggers.

RepresentsResource.description: Resource lifeline to the physical resource whose timeline it represents.

TriggersResourceInteraction.description: Event to the objectified interaction it triggers.

ResourceInteractionRelatesFunction.description: Objectified interaction to the resource function it relates to.

TracesInformationModel.description: Data model to information model traced.

RepresentsDataProduct.description: Data model to the actual data product it represents.

AggregatesDataEntity.description: Whole data entity to a constituent entity.

AggregatesDataAttribute.description: Data entity to a member attribute.

HasPhysicalCharacteristic.description: Data entity or attribute to its physical characteristic.

ConstrainsResource.description: Resource requirement or constraint to the subject it applies to.

TracesLogicalConstraint.description: Resource constraint to logical constraint traced.

OriginatesFromResourceRationale.description: Resource constraint to the rationale it originates from.

ResourceRationaleOriginatesFromLogical.description: Resource rationale to the logical constraint it originates from.

DeliversResourceReadiness.description: Configuration to delivered resource readiness level.

TracesLogicalReadiness.description: Resource readiness to logical readiness traced.

ResourceReadinessDeliversConfiguration.description: Readiness level to the capability configuration it delivers in Pr.

ResourceMilestoneCorrespondsToLogical.description: Resource milestone to a corresponding logical milestone.

DefinesResourceEvolution.description: Project to the capability configuration whose evolution it defines.

DefinesGlossaryTerm.description: Architecture description to relevant glossary term.

CharacterizesArchitectureDescription.description: Glossary term, contextual data or metadata to the description it characterizes. Metadata includes its UAF subtype ArchitectureMetadata.

StandardDescribesContext.description: Standard to contextual data it describes.

ContainsView.description: Architecture description to constituent view. Same direction as ADMBw ViewsInArchitecturalDescription.

ConformsToViewpoint.description: View to governing viewpoint (also retain the native viewpoint reference).

GovernsView.description: Viewpoint to its governed view in the NAF cut-out.

StakeholderHasConcern.description: Stakeholder to concern. Same direction as ADMBw StakeholderConcern.

FramesConcern.description: Viewpoint to framed concern. Same direction as ADMBw ConcernForViewpoint.

CorrespondenceRelatesElement.description: Correspondence to an architecture-description element or description.

ExtendsMethodology.description: Methodology to a methodology it extends. A MethodologyExtension can retain its rationale.

DocumentsArchitectureProject.description: Architecture description to the project it documents.

MethodologyAppliesStandard.description: Methodology to a standard it applies.

ArchitectureStatusDescribesProduct.description: Status to the work product it describes.

ArchitectureDescriptionGeneralization.description: Architectural description to its generalized work product.

WorkProductContainsView.description: Work product to a contained view.

ProductHasVersion.description: Work product to its version or baseline in the cut-out.

ArchitectureVersionSupersedes.description: Newer version to the earlier version it supersedes.

ArchitectureVersionGeneralization.description: Baseline to its generalized architecture version.

GroupsMeasure.description: Measure group to a member measure or nested group.

GovernsMetric.description: Measure to desired or achieved metric it governs.

StandardSpecifiesMeasure.description: Standard to the measure it specifies.

MeasureAssessesArchitecture.description: Measure to the architecture description it assesses.

GroupsStandard.description: Group to member standard or nested group.

StandardGeneralization.description: Specialized standard to its general standard.

IncludesArchitecturalConstraint.description: Standards profile to an included architecture constraint.

DefinesArchitectureEvolution.description: Project to status whose evolution it defines.

ArchitectureMilestoneCorrespondence.description: Architecture milestone to another domain milestone or a planning enterprise phase.

OperationalControlFlow.description: Control flow between L4 operational activity definitions or between native UAF operational activity actions. Both endpoints must use the same representation.
